accepted.s: Which of the following institutions jointly steers the National Supercomputing Mission?
accepted.x: The mission is jointly steered by the Department of Science and Technology and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct pair of nodal agencies rather than the implementing institutions.
accepted.sec: National Supercomputing Mission - PARAM systems, agencies, AIRAWAT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The supercomputers established under the National Supercomputing Mission are linked through the National Supercomputing Grid over the:
accepted.x: The systems are linked on the National Supercomputing Grid over the National Knowledge Network.
accepted.tq: Test the exact network name and reject nearby connectivity terms.
accepted.sec: National Supercomputing Mission - PARAM systems, agencies, AIRAWAT  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the status of the National Supercomputing Mission:
1. Forty systems with aggregate capacity exceeding 64 PF are planned.
2. Thirty-seven systems have been commissioned with 39 PF at 37 locations.
3. Three additional systems of about 27 PF are based on the indigenous RUDRA server.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the status and planned expansion of the mission as reflected in the 2026 update.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical statement separately, especially the distinction between planned and commissioned systems.
accepted.sec: National Supercomputing Mission - PARAM systems, agencies, AIRAWAT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The additional National Supercomputing Mission systems include a National Facility of approximately:
accepted.x: The additional systems include a National Facility of approximately 20 PF.
accepted.tq: Use the embedded figure within a larger capacity estimate.
accepted.sec: National Supercomputing Mission - PARAM systems, agencies, AIRAWAT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the indigenous technology stack of the National Supercomputing Mission?
o: Rudra server board, Trinetra interconnect and AlmaLinux software
AUM processor, Vajra interconnect and Ubuntu software only
PARAM board, Shakti interconnect and Windows software
Rudra board, Garuda interconnect and proprietary software exclusively
accepted.x: The indigenous stack comprises the Rudra server board, Trinetra interconnect and open-source AlmaLinux software.
accepted.tq: Match the technical components as a complete stack and beware of the ‘exclusively’ trap.
accepted.sec: National Supercomputing Mission - PARAM systems, agencies, AIRAWAT  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (System)
 a. PARAM Shivay
 b. PARAM Porul
 c. PARAM Pravega
 d. PARAM Ananta

List-II (Host)
 i. IISc Bengaluru
 ii. IIT Gandhinagar
 iii. IIT (BHU)
 iv. NIT Tiruchirappalli

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
accepted.x: PARAM Shivay is at IIT (BHU), PARAM Porul at NIT Tiruchirappalli, PARAM Pravega at IISc Bengaluru and PARAM Ananta at IIT Gandhinagar.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure machine–host pair and eliminate codes containing a wrong pair.
accepted.sec: National Supercomputing Mission - PARAM systems, agencies, AIRAWAT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: PARAM Kamrupa is hosted at IIT Guwahati. PARAM Shakti is at IIT Madras, PARAM Rudra systems are at Pune, Delhi and Kolkata, and AIRAWAT is at C-DAC, Pune.
accepted.tq: Find the correctly matched pair among closely related supercomputing hosts.
accepted.sec: National Supercomputing Mission - PARAM systems, agencies, AIRAWAT  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about PARAM Shakti:
1. It is located at IIT Madras.
2. It has a capacity of 3.1 PF.
3. Forty per cent of its capacity is available to outside researchers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: PARAM Shakti is at IIT Madras, has 3.1 PF capacity and reserves 40 per cent capacity for outside researchers.
accepted.tq: Combine location, capacity and usage-share facts in a coded statement question.
accepted.sec: National Supercomputing Mission - PARAM systems, agencies, AIRAWAT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Rudra server from the AUM programme?
o: AUM is the interconnect used in all PARAM systems, whereas Rudra is a software platform.
Rudra is a server board used for the mission, whereas AUM is a separate C-DAC HPC chip programme.
Rudra is an HPC chip programme, whereas AUM is the mission’s open-source operating system.
Both Rudra and AUM are names of the same processor.
accepted.x: The Rudra machines are built on the Rudra server, while AUM is a separate C-DAC high-performance computing chip programme.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between look-alike technical names by identifying their different functions.
accepted.sec: National Supercomputing Mission - PARAM systems, agencies, AIRAWAT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: AIRAWAT, the artificial-intelligence supercomputer associated with the National Supercomputing Mission, is located at:
accepted.x: AIRAWAT is located at C-DAC, Pune.
accepted.tq: Test the host institution of a named machine rather than its ranking.
accepted.sec: National Supercomputing Mission - PARAM systems, agencies, AIRAWAT  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the National Quantum Mission?
o: A MeitY mission with an outlay of ₹10,371.92 crore for 2024–29
A DBT mission with an outlay of ₹4,077 crore for five years
A MoES mission with an outlay of ₹76,000 crore for 2021–26
A DST mission with an outlay of ₹6,003.65 crore for 2023–24 to 2030–31
accepted.x: The mission is under DST, has an outlay of ₹6,003.65 crore and covers eight years from 2023–24 to 2030–31.
accepted.tq: Compare mission ministry, outlay and period together to avoid cross-matching with other missions.
accepted.sec: National Quantum Mission - approval, outlay, hubs, qubit targets  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Quantum Mission aims to develop intermediate-scale quantum computers containing approximately:
accepted.x: The target is intermediate-scale computers with 50 to 1000 physical qubits within eight years.
accepted.tq: Use the exact numerical range and distinguish physical qubits from logical qubits.
accepted.sec: National Quantum Mission - approval, outlay, hubs, qubit targets  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following are targets or technological areas of the National Quantum Mission?
1. Satellite QKD over 2000 km within India
2. Inter-city QKD over 2000 km
3. Quantum links with other countries
4. Development of magnetometers and atomic clocks
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
accepted.x: All four listed areas form part of the National Quantum Mission’s targets and technological objectives.
accepted.tq: Use the all-inclusive option only after verifying every listed application.

accepted.s:
Match the thematic hub of the National Quantum Mission with its host:

List-I (Thematic hub)

 b. Quantum Communication
 c. Quantum Sensing and Metrology
 d. Quantum Materials and Devices

List-II (Host)
 i. IIT Delhi
 ii. IIT Bombay

accepted.sec: National Quantum Mission - approval, outlay, hubs, qubit targets  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Central Fabrication Facilities under the National Quantum Mission are located at:
o: IIT Madras, IIT Guwahati, IIT Delhi and BARC
IIT Delhi, IISc, IIT Bombay and IIT Kanpur
IISc, IIT Hyderabad, IIT Kanpur and ISRO
IIT Bombay, IIT Roorkee, NAL and DRDO

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with a start-up supported under the National Quantum Mission?
o: QNu Labs — 500 km QKD network and QShield
accepted.x: QNu Labs is associated with a 500 km QKD network and QShield. QpiAI is associated with a 64-qubit QPU, PQuest with a Quantum Diamond Microscope, and Prenishq with a diode laser.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Launch of the National Supercomputing Mission
B. Approval of the National Quantum Mission
C. Approval of the Deep Ocean Mission
D. Introduction of the Bio-E3 Policy

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
accepted.x: The National Supercomputing Mission was launched in 2015, the Deep Ocean Mission was approved in 2021, the National Quantum Mission in 2023 and the Bio-E3 Policy was introduced in 2024.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the middle approvals by year.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Deep Ocean Mission:
1. It is under the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
2. It was approved in June 2021.
3. It has an outlay of ₹4,077 crore over five years.
4. It is one of the nine PM-STIAC missions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The mission is also intended to support the blue economy.
accepted.tq: Verify ministry, approval date, outlay and institutional classification separately.
accepted.sec: Deep Ocean Mission - ministry, components, Samudrayaan  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated focus or implication of the Deep Ocean Mission?
o: Development of quantum computers with 50–1000 qubits
Multiple focus areas including Samudrayaan-related activities
accepted.x: Quantum computing targets belong to the National Quantum Mission, not the Deep Ocean Mission. The Deep Ocean Mission supports the blue economy and deep-sea exploration and mining.
accepted.tq: Find the out-of-domain statement by separating ocean objectives from quantum objectives.
accepted.sec: Deep Ocean Mission - ministry, components, Samudrayaan  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about Samudrayaan is correct?
o: It involves a four-member crewed aircraft for atmospheric exploration up to 6000 km.
It is a bio-manufacturing programme for marine organisms.
It is a satellite QKD mission designed for a 2000 km link.
It involves Matsya 6000, an indigenous submersible for a three-member crew and a depth target of 6000 m.
accepted.x: Samudrayaan involves the indigenous Matsya 6000 submersible, designed for a three-member crew, deep-sea mining and exploration, with a target depth of 6000 m.
accepted.tq: Identify the mission from its vehicle, crew size, purpose and depth target.
accepted.sec: Deep Ocean Mission - ministry, components, Samudrayaan  [other exams]

Biotechnology for Employment, Electronics and Education

o: It is a DBT programme approved in 2024 with an outlay of ₹10,000 crore.
It is an MoES programme approved in 2021 with an outlay of ₹4,077 crore.
